The Sheriff's Office provides 24-hour security in and around the judicial complex. Last year, courthouse deputies screened approximately 350,000 individuals who entered the courthouse. Approximately 90% of the people who entered the courthouse are there for court purposes.

Courtroom security. There are 16 courtrooms in the Judicial Center. Soon there will be 18. We are the second busiest courthouse in Virginia. A courtroom deputy provides security and maintains order in the courtroom.

They also provide support to the judges and clerks, manage the courtroom jurors, and handle additional court-related tasks as duties as required. When there is a high-profile case, additional screening and staff is required, along with other restrictions.
In the past year, we had 60 high-profile cases. The Sheriff's Office public safety to communicators dispatch calls for service in the judicial complex.

They receive and process all the calls for my office. Our public safety communicators are required to complete dispatch basic training. Additionally, they are required to maintain VCN Level A certification throughout the Virginia Criminal Information Network.

They monitor over 200 cameras to assist courthouse deputies. They monitor and dispatch 50 emergency alarms throughout the courthouse. They track the movement of inmates throughout the courthouse daily. All transportation, civil process, and other units communicate with the sheriff's office dispatchers.

Deputies assigned to vertical deployment receive inmates from the adult detention center for court. Inmates are then escorted to and from courtrooms within the courthouse. Inmates remain in our custody and are returned to the adult detention center to serve their sentence, remain in custody pending a court date, all released.

They also take into custody persons committed to the adult detention center and process them for transfers. In FY23, this section handled over 24,000 inmates. The live scan section is responsible for mandated processing.

Persons committed of certain offenses are processed and DNA is collected and sent to the state forensic laboratory. Persons released by the police on a summons for certain minor offenses are processed by this section after their court appearance.

They assist people requesting fingerprint for job applications. This section also conduct background checks for citizens applying for concealed weapons permits. In FY23, we conducted 6,754 background checks, and in FY24, we conducted 4,093 background checks thus far this year.

The background checks are done to assist the clerk of the court in issuing concealed weapons permits. On to our civil process section. Deputies assigned to civil process serve legal documents within Prince William County and the cities of Manassas and Manassas Park.

Most documents we serve are posted on the property, but some require personal service and oftentimes very consuming. That means that deputies sometimes have to go back to their residence and look for people on several occasions.

In FY23, deputies serve 64,920 documents, and in FY24, deputies serve 49,358 documents thus far in FY24. When an emergency call comes for service, is dispatched, a deputy will respond to the call if they're in the area.

In other words, we have deputies all over the county, and if a call comes out for service, they will assist the police officers and back them up. Deputies back up police officers during traffic stops when needed direct traffic at a crash scene.

Civil process deputies are very busy. There are several documents we serve that require two deputies. Two of those documents are levies and evictions. In FY23, we executed 216 levies, and in FY24, we executed 134 levies thus far.

In FY23, we executed 2,664 evictions, and in FY24, we executed 1,679 evictions thus far. Funeral escorts are not a mandated responsibility, but as your sheriff, I believe it is absolutely necessary to provide this service to our community.

This office received many favorable comments concerning funeral escorts from the public. In FY23, this section performed 390 funeral escorts, and in FY24, this section performed 231 funeral escorts thus far.

The method we provide and conduct for funeral escorts sends a message to our community and visitors about who we are as an agency in Prince William County and the cities of Manassas and Manassas Park. Transportation to and from criminal justice facilities is a challenging daily event, mainly because of the distance to other jails and facilities within the state.
